observation: REWORK-PROGRESS needed approvals for rev 6 and rev 7 although only the base commit was wrong: rev 5 and rev 6 were planned with abbreviated --base-commit values (93283d9, 7e7da68) that workflow plan stored unchecked; the human approved rev 6 and enter then refused it ('requires an exact Git base commit'). BASE-COMMIT-EXACT rev 1 then needed a scope-only rev 2 because tests/WorkflowPlanCommandTest.php asserted the old behaviour and was not in scope.

evidence.summary: Observed passed with exit code 0 for implementation sha256:3d11fdd4c2d6c2654ff9664453bf7b365e48d8c4ba7100d1af34a8ddfcdaf33b.

hypothesis: Approval rounds are wasted when a Contract can reach the approval card in a state execution will refuse, or when existing tests that pin the changed behaviour are outside the proposed scope; deterministic checks before approval prevent both without weakening the gate.
validated_conclusion: Fixed the first cause in code: plan now resolves --base-commit to the exact commit or refuses it (PR #1178, regression plan->approve->standard->enter fails before and passes after). The second cause remains: a pre-approval scope check that runs the existing tests or Map references against the proposed scope (TASK-REFINEMENT) is the next executable improvement; also the approval card reports 'No Contract field changed' when only base_commit changed.
